author: rkulkarni
body: The loss depends on the output, but the output depends on every earlier z through the activations. Each layer's output is sigma(z), so when the chain rule passes through a layer it picks up sigma'(z). Write the derivative for a two-layer network by hand once and you'll see it appear exactly once per layer.

body: Also helps to remember why ReLU trains faster: its derivative is 1 for positive inputs, so the gradient doesn't shrink layer by layer like it does with sigmoid.

author: sneha
body: Prevention breaks one of the four necessary conditions up front (like no hold-and-wait), so deadlock is structurally impossible. Avoidance allows all four conditions but checks every request at runtime and only grants it if the system stays in a safe state. Banker's is avoidance.

author: miyer
body: Good answer. For the exam, also mention that avoidance needs to know maximum resource needs in advance, which is why it's rare in real operating systems.

author: ishita
body: An eigenvector is a direction that the matrix only stretches, never rotates. In PCA, the covariance matrix's eigenvectors are the directions where data varies the most, and the eigenvalues tell you how much. Keep the top few and you've reduced dimensions while keeping most of the information.
